content.text: The Moon, the fifth largest solar system satellite, holds a special place in our hearts. So how far is the Moon? However, On average, the Moon is located at around 384,400 kilometers away from Earth. You could fit 30 entire earth between us and the moon. Or You could fit every single planet in the solar system. The Moon can get as far as 406,700 km away from Earth and as close as 356,400 km away. On average, it would take you around three days to get to the Moon. The first manned spacecraft Apollo 11 mission, arrived in just 51 hours and 49 minutes, Even now, Neil Armstrong’s team remains the fastest crew to get to the Moon on a spacecraft. The slowest mission, to the Moon, was ESA’s SMART-1. The lunar probe reached the Moon in 1 year, one month, and two weeks. As the probe used an ion engine as a propellant, using only 82 kg of xenon for the entire mission, it remains the most fuel-efficient mission in history. The Moon, due to gravitational interactions with our Earth, is drifting away from us at around 4 cm / 1.5 inches every year. Because of this, the estimated distance is always changing.
